Rebuilding the car, looping the rest

Three independent car renders are being drawn and judged blind, because the vehicle was the biggest gap in three separate critiques. In parallel, five pieces are in builder/critic loops.

Benchmark access

tesla.com cannot be reached from this build sandbox: Tesla's edge (Akamai) blocks the datacenter IP for direct requests and for every public screenshot service tried, web.archive.org is blocked by this environment's egress policy, and Chromium here has no outbound HTTPS at all. Live side-by-side capture of the real funnel is therefore impossible from inside this session. Critics score against docs/reference-spec.md — the Tesla funnel written down as measurable properties — plus their own knowledge of that funnel, and every round must still name the single largest remaining gap.

Hero Full-viewport model section, headline, CTAs In review 1 The vehicle — the largest object in the frame at roughly 940×320px, 65% of the viewport width — is shaded as flat vector facets, not as a studio-lit product render. Two ruler-straight light-gray stripes run the full length of the flank at a constant y≈408 and y≈418 from x≈575 to x≈1140, cutting straight across what should be a curved door skin; the hood and roof are each a single flat fill separated by hard polygon seams (a straight crease from the A-pillar base down to the nose at x≈300); and there is no continuous tonal roll from the shoulder to the rocker. The result reads as clip-art dropped on a gradient, which is exactly the thing the benchmark hero never does.

Listing grid Inventory cards and layout Revising 1 The image plate — the largest element on every card at 318×187px — shows a flat side-elevation silhouette with a mirrored floor reflection, so the car reads as a two-tone vector sticker rather than a photographed object: the body is a single flat fill, the glasshouse one black band, the wheels black discs, the lights a white dash and a red dash, and three of the six visible cards are the same sedan outline in grey/blue/grey. The benchmark's inventory plate is a studio three-quarter render with modelled sheet metal, so at 1440px the candidate's results grid reads as clip art on a template while the benchmark reads as product photography.

Checkout form Fields, validation, order placement Revising 1 The "Your Vehicle" plate — the single image on a $33,130 checkout and the largest element on the page at 720x264 — renders the car sitting on a hard-edged black rectangle. Measured in checkout-desktop-full.png: a pure-black mass (#131415) spans x=275→729 (455px) with a razor-flat bottom at y=597 and square 90° vertical ends at both x=275 and x=729, i.e. it runs the entire length of the car under the sill and terminates outboard of the tyre contact patches instead of tucking behind the bumpers. The tyres visibly sit on top of the brick rather than on the floor. The benchmark's checkout shows a photographic studio render of the exact configuration; this reads as 2008 vector clipart, and it is the first thing a shopper sees under the first section heading.
